name: CPU cores and ABI
plain: Reads core count and CPU architecture with no prompt.
meaning: Identifies chipset class (4 to 10 cores). A device-model proxy: apps pick builds and thread pools with it, trackers add it to a fingerprint.

android.api_surface: Runtime.availableProcessors(), Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS (API 21), /proc/cpuinfo (restricted per app on newer builds)
android.note: Core count 4 to 10; ABI arm64-v8a on nearly all current phones

ios.api_surface: Cores 2 to 10 on iPhone; arm64 only

limits.headline: Can see how many CPU cores your phone has and what chip type, with no prompt
limits.user_action: Nothing. The app checks when it starts, often to pick graphics or video settings
can: See the number of cores, typically 4 to 10 on Android and 2 to 10 on iPhone
See the chip type; nearly all current phones are 64 bit ARM
Pick lighter or heavier settings to match your phone
cannot: See detailed chip info on newer Android, where per-app limits block parts of CPU info files
Learn who you are from core count alone
Change how fast the chip runs

story.what_it_is: An app can see how many processor cores your phone has and what chip type.
story.for_you: You never see this check. Apps use it to decide how hard to work your phone. It also shows how powerful or old your phone is.
story.for_makers: Makers pick graphics quality and how many tasks to run at once. Trackers add core count to a device fingerprint, since it is a stable detail.

use_cases.example: A 3D game picks high graphics on an eight core phone and low graphics on a four core phone.
A video editor uses all cores to render a clip faster, and fewer on weak phones.
A streaming app picks a video decoder that fits your chip.
An AR app turns off heavy effects on phones with few cores so tracking stays smooth.
An ad firm adds core count to a device fingerprint.
A developer builds a different app file for each chip type to keep the download small.

risks: Shows how new your phone is
story.android_note: Read through system properties with no prompt, including the chip type.
story.ios_note: Read through system calls with no prompt.
